key_insight: In a retrospective simulation, Sybil identified 33.8% of negative lung cancer screens for biennial screening with no delayed cancers observed.
clinical_relevance: AI-guided screening intervals could reduce radiology workload and expand screening capacity, but require prospective validation before clinical adoption.
method: Evaluated Sybil using 3,120 lung cancer screening exams from a tertiary safety-net hospital.
Analyzed risk prediction in Lung-RADS 1/2 cases and other subgroups.
Simulated biennial screening using Sybil and Brock risk scores calibrated on an NLST subset.
evidence_signal: Sybil's 2-year AUC was 0.746 in Lung-RADS 1/2 cases; the cohort had 72 cancers and median follow-up of 2.3 years.
watch_item: The single-center retrospective simulation and limited follow-up do not establish the safety of extending screening intervals in practice.
paper_title: Investigating AI's potential in risk-stratifying lung cancer screenings for extending screening intervals and reducing workload: A retrospective analysis of a tertiary hospital cohort
